tagline: Up Lehman Creek to the cave a rancher showed off.
intro: In Baker, Highway 488 turns west off Baker Road and runs five miles up toward Great Basin National Park, roughly following Lehman Creek through desert country. As a state route it ends at a cattle guard just short of the Lehman Caves Visitor Center.
An earlier track ran more to the northeast and met Baker Road north of town. By 1942 the road had its present line, and it was paved by 1949.

moments.title: Baker
moments.text: A town of a few dozen people, named for an early settler, George W. Baker, that counts the inventor of the atomic force microscope, Calvin Quate, among its own.

moments.title: Lehman Caves
moments.text: A rancher, Absalom Lehman, began guiding visitors into the cave in 1885, and inscriptions left by visitors before it became a national monument in 1922 are in the cave still.

moments.title: Wheeler Peak
moments.text: At treeline near the 13,063-foot peak stood a bristlecone pine at least 5,000 years old, the oldest nonclonal organism ever found, until it was cut down for research in 1964.

practical: The park service warns that navigation apps can route drivers to remote parts of the park, and advises routing to the Lehman Caves Visitor Center or to Baker.
